30.0.0.en: God declares Himself as the God of Israel, that is, its Shepherd and Defender, and commands Jeremiah to write His coming prophecies in this chapter, because these prophecies will be fulfilled after a time and not now; but He declares them now to give hope to His people, captive and humiliated under the hand of Babylon. Chapters 30-33 are a message of consolation to encourage the people, full of hope.

30.1.0.en: God promises His people to bring them back from captivity. Although they had been divided into two kingdoms, Israel and Judah, after enduring the affliction of captivity the two become one kingdom after the captivity, to possess the Promised Land as a gift from God. The return from captivity is a renewal of their possession of it, after they had lost it through captivity because of their sins. They possess it from God and so thank Him, and it does not possess them, that is, it does not take hold of their hearts by its material things.

30.1.1.en: Accept affliction for God's sake, purify your heart in it, and forgive those who wronged you, so that love may return and reign over your heart, and you may possess many virtues which God grants you.

30.2.s.en: (2) Salvation by the hand of the Medes and Persians

30.2.0.en: This prophecy concerns the kingdoms of Israel and Judah, which were exposed to captivity, and He wants to give them hope of deliverance from this affliction. He begins with Israel because it was carried captive first and has suffered for a long time the pains of bondage.

30.3.0.en: He expresses the feelings of the captives in Babylon when they heard of the attack of the Medes and Persians upon it. They feared greatly because they were humiliated under the hand of Babylon, and they felt a new affliction coming upon them, the attack of the Medes.

30.4.0.en: His loins: his belly and middle.

30.4.1.en: In travail: a woman whose delivery is near and who is in pain.

30.4.2.en: He likens the fear of the captive men, when they put their hands on their middle, to a woman whose delivery is near and who suffers her pains... And he says, does a man lay an egg like a hen, or give birth like a woman? Of course not, but it is the appearance of intense fear, which also showed on the faces that turned yellow as the blood fled from them because of terror.

30.5.0.en: God reassures His people, the descendants of Jacob, that although this day is difficult, the day of the Medes' and Persians' attack on Babylon to destroy it and kill those in it, among whom were the Jews, God will turn this day into salvation for His people; for after Cyrus, the first of the kings of the Medes and Persians, took possession, he ordered the return of the captive Jews to Jerusalem.

30.6.0.en: His yoke: a crosswise piece of wood placed on the necks of the two animals that draw the farming implements.

30.6.1.en: Thy bonds: the rope with which the yoke is tied on the neck of the beast.

30.6.2.en: God gives His people the good news that by the attack of the Medes and Persians the people of God are freed from the bondage of captivity and return to Jerusalem and begin worship in the temple, which signifies faith in Christ and worshiping Him in the Church. Then no one enslaves the people of God, since they have been freed from sin, and sin does not enslave them afterward; that is, strangers, who are the demons, cannot enslave them. The people of God were delivered by the Medes and Persians from captivity, but after a time the Greek kingdom arose and enslaved them, and after it the Roman kingdom, so deliverance from bondage was temporary; but spiritual salvation by faith in Christ lasts forever.

30.7.0.en: David their king: Christ, who is of the seed of David.

30.7.1.en: With the return of the people of God from captivity to Jerusalem, they began the worship of God in the temple, which was a preparation for their faith in Christ, who is of the seed of David, so that they serve Him forever with praise.

30.7.2.en: Do not be troubled by the afflictions that pass through your life, for they are the beginning of many blessings you will receive and they free you from many sins that enslave you, and you set out in worship and love, and enjoy fellowship with God more than before.

30.8.s.en: (3) Healing from wounds that cannot be cured

30.8.0.en: God repeats His promise that He will deliver His people from the Babylonian captivity and bring them back to Jerusalem and Judea, and He calls it "My servant" to declare His responsibility for it, so that it may trust in God's promise and be reassured despite the afflictions surrounding it in captivity.

30.9.0.en: God affirms His care and concern for His people and His promise of salvation to them, and reassures them that He punishes the nations that carry them captive and destroys them for their evils, while His people He disciplines only that they may repent, and then He saves them.

30.10.0.en: The splint: a support for a fracture in the bones by means of pieces of wood or plaster so that the fracture knits. Grievous: hard and severe and impossible to heal.

30.10.1.en: God makes clear His feeling of the harshness of Babylon's bondage to His people, which is like a break in the bones that no splint can heal, or a very deep wound from which recovery is impossible. But despite the impossibility of escaping the bondage of Babylon, God, who is able to do all things, intervenes and delivers them; He makes clear the difficulty of the situation in order to show the power of His salvation.

30.11.0.en: Pressing: squeezing the part afflicted with deep pus to bring out the pus within it and clean it.

30.11.2.en: Healing plaster: a strip of cloth (gauze) bound on the wound after the medicines are put on it. He also shows the misery and humiliation of the bondage of his people in Babylon, likening them to a person with pus in his body who finds no one to treat him and bring it out, for he has no medicines or cloths with which to bind his wounds; he is gravely ill and has no one to treat him or any medicines that would help him.

30.12.0.en: Because of the harshness of the bondage, which is a severe discipline from God, the people of God not only suffered but everyone who had shown them an old friendship, such as Egypt, kept away from them, which increased the feeling of despair within the people of God, and nothing remained but hope in God alone.

30.13.0.en: God addresses His people as a rejected bride and says to her: Do not cry out asking for someone to heal you, for there is no healing for your wounds, that is, no hope of your deliverance according to human thought, since God is the One who struck you, so who can rescue you from His hand unless you offer repentance, and He forgives you and lifts it from you.

30.14.1.en: When the people of God repent, their God delivers them by humbling those who humbled them, who were devouring them by killing them to wipe them out: they themselves are exposed to death and to captivity to far-off lands, their spoils are seized and their houses plundered. This is what actually happened to the Babylonians when the Medes and Persians attacked them.

30.15.0.en: God promises to heal her incurable wounds, healing her by His power which is able to do all things; she will no longer be called exiled and captive, but returns as His bride to her land, that is, to Jerusalem.

30.15.1.en: If you are passing through hard afflictions with no hope of resolution, or unbearable problems, do not be troubled, because your God watches over everything. He will heal you, treat your problems and lift every affliction from you, so that you praise Him always.

30.16.s.en: (4) The return to Jerusalem and the change of conditions

30.16.0.en: The people of God left the tents in which they dwelt during the captivity and returned to Jerusalem to build its walls and palaces and dwell in them, and to bless God, who restored glory to Jerusalem, built on a high hill.

30.17.0.en: The people praise God, and the children go out to play in the streets, rejoicing in their city. God blesses them so that they multiply and their number increases, and gives them standing and greatness among the peoples.

30.18.0.en: The people of God return to their strength and standing in Jerusalem, and whoever among the surrounding peoples tries to trouble them, God punishes.

30.19.0.en: Engaged his heart: he gave up his heart's attachment to material things, relied on God and held fast to Him; that is, he sold himself to the love of God.

30.19.1.en: Among God's blessings upon them is that one of themselves rules them and not enemies, serving as governor over them like Zerubbabel, Nehemiah or Judas Maccabeus; and God promises to bless their ruler because he drew near to God and asked His help and blessing.

30.20.0.en: In the end the people of God enjoy His care and fatherhood, and become a people peculiar to Him, and He is their God who defends them.

30.20.1.en: God is able to restore your glory to you, honor you and bless you, however much sin has wearied you, the sin you held to and which caused you any losses. Your God is rich and loves you, and He will compensate you for everything as long as you have returned to Him.

30.21.0.en: A continuing whirlwind: a violent wind that sweeps away everything in its path.

30.21.1.en: God declares that He has allowed a severe whirlwind and tempest which express His wrath that He pours out on the wicked, namely the Babylonians who humiliated His people. God allowed this discipline for His people so that they would repent, but afterward He disciplines those who disciplined them and were harsh to them, namely the Babylonians.

30.22.0.en: The latter days: after the accomplishment of His purposes, that is, after the collapse of Babylon and the return of His people from captivity. God declares that His wrath will not cease against Babylon until it collapses, and the kingdom of the Medes and Persians comes and restores His people to their land.

30.22.1.en: If you do not understand God's purposes in the afflictions that pass through your life, know that He will make them clear to you afterward; but trust in His fatherhood, which cares for you and permits nothing for you except for the salvation of your soul.

31.0.0.en: At the same time: the return from captivity, or faith in Christ.

31.0.2.en: God promises to bring His people back from captivity, so that they are one people and He is their God. This also signifies the faith of, not only the tribes of Israel, but the whole world in Christ, so that they become one people, the new Israel.

31.1.0.en: The people which were left of the sword: those who were not killed and did not die in captivity.

31.1.1.en: God speaks of His people scattered in the world in the bondage of captivity, far from their land as though in a wilderness, and declares that they have found grace in the eyes of God. God shows His love in that He is the One who takes the initiative to give His people rest, saying "I went to cause him to rest"; for God is the One who goes after His children to free them from the bondage of sin if they repent and cry to Him, and this is the meaning of the affliction of captivity or of any affliction we pass through.

31.2.0.en: The captive people felt that God was far from them, so God declares that He appeared to His people, whom He thought far from Him although He is very near to them, and it is He who allowed their discipline that they might repent. He even declares that His love for His people is everlasting, that is, it does not pass away but continues forever. Therefore, if He allows them affliction and discipline, He returns and has mercy on them; indeed He is ready to have mercy on them many times as long as they repent and return to Him. Mercy is perpetual, that is, it continues throughout life.

31.3.0.en: God continues His promises, speaking of His people as His virgin, that is, His bride, and promises to build her again, and moreover she will be adorned with joy and rejoice like one who plays musical instruments and dances like the players in the dancing grounds; that is, His people praise Him with joy.

31.4.0.en: Shall eat them as common things: they rise early, that is, they get up energetically from early morning to work.

31.4.1.en: God also promises her fertility and good things: vineyards will be planted in Samaria, the capital of Israel, and the farmers rise early with energy to plant the trees and gather the fruit. This signifies the spiritual fruits with which the children of God are adorned.

31.5.0.en: The watchmen: the guards, that is, the servants.

31.5.1.en: There shall be a day: the day of the return from captivity.

31.5.2.en: After their return from captivity, they all worship God in Jerusalem, that is, Zion, because they have been disciplined by the affliction of captivity and have returned to God with all their hearts. The servants do their work, which is calling all the people to the worship of God.

31.5.3.en: If only you would understand that affliction is a temporary period which God allows for you to review yourself, bind yourself to Him and renew your vows, and then you will enjoy God's infinite love, His wide mercy and His beautiful promises.

31.6.0.en: God calls the peoples of the world to rejoice and sing for His people, who are the chief of the peoples because of their faith in God. He also calls His people to praise Him and asks them to be saved. God wants to save His people, but He waits for them to repent and seek Him, and then He saves them from all their enemies and gladdens them from all their hearts.

31.7.0.en: God also promises that He will gather His people scattered in the north at Babylon and from the ends of the world, however weak they are because of the humiliation of bondage. He expresses this weakness in four states: "the blind," that is, one who has lost the ability to discern and needs someone to lead him; the second state is "the lame," unable to walk except with the help of another; the third state is "the woman with child," who walks slowly because of her pregnancy; and the fourth state is "her that travaileth," that is, one who has come into birth pains and is unable to walk. God gathers His people in great numbers with all their weakness and delivers them and brings them back to their land.

31.8.0.en: From the abundance of affliction, the people weep to God and make supplication to Him to save them, so He brings them out of captivity by His power and leads them in clear, straight ways full of water, that is, life, which signifies the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church, to which unbelievers return and find their salvation.

31.8.1.en: And as God leads them they do not grow weary on the way or fall, for He keeps them.

31.8.2.en: All this shows the fatherhood of God toward His people, whom He considers His firstborn among the peoples of the earth. When He says "Ephraim," He means all His people, because Ephraim possessed a large region in the Promised Land. The people of God in the Old Testament were the firstborn, but in the New Testament, as all peoples believe, the believers in Christ are in all the countries of the world.

31.9.0.en: God addresses the peoples of the earth because He wants the salvation of all, and began with His people the children of Israel as an example so that all may come to Him. He says to all the peoples that if He has scattered His people by captivity in order to discipline them so that they repent, then He returns and gathers them and delivers them from the bondage of captivity.

31.10.0.en: Here He clearly declares His redemption of His people and their deliverance from the hand of Babylon, which is far stronger than His people. All this is a symbol of Christ's redemption of mankind on the Cross and its deliverance from the hand of one stronger than it, namely Satan.

31.11.0.en: Zion: a Hebrew name meaning fortress; it is one of the summits of the hills on which Jerusalem was built, and by Zion is meant all of Jerusalem.

31.11.2.en: When the people of God reach Jerusalem, which is Zion built on a high hill, they sing with joy at their return to their land, and God pours out on them many blessings from the produce of the field such as wheat, and from trees such as the vines from which they take wine, and the olives from which they take oil. He also blesses their cattle, the sheep and the oxen, so they are many, and their land becomes like a garden from the abundance of water, fertility and many good things. God does not allow them captivity afterward and assimilation among the peoples of the earth, and this is what actually happened, for the children of Israel were not carried captive again until the coming of Christ, in whom all the previous types are fulfilled, who gives the believers in Him many spiritual blessings, and their souls become like a garden, that is, they become temples of the Holy Spirit.

31.12.0.en: He expresses the joy of His children after their return from captivity by the young women of His people who dance, and the young men and the old whose weeping during the captivity turns to joy. He also likens His people to a virgin who rejoices like a bride in her bridegroom, and God also shows His fatherhood by comforting His children and compensating them for all they endured in captivity. This signifies God's comforts to His children in heaven, compensating them for all their toils on earth.

31.13.0.en: The people turn to the worship of God and offer many sacrifices in His house, from which the priests take their share and are satisfied; thus God satisfies the people with all their leaders. This signifies the Holy Spirit's satisfying of the believers, the priests and the servants by His work in the Church, and He gives special blessings to the priests for their pastoral responsibility in leading the people.

31.13.1.en: Thank God for His gifts and praise Him in His Church and in every place, so that you feel His presence with you and are occupied with Him rather than with every sin and the various enticements of the world.

31.13.2.en: (3) The end of the pains of captivity (vv. 15-20)

31.13.3.en: 15- Thus saith the LORD; A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rahel weeping for her children refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not. 16- Thus saith the LORD; Refrain thy voice from weeping, and thine eyes from tears: for thy work shall be rewarded, saith the LORD; and they shall come again from the land of the enemy. 17- And there is hope in thine end, saith the LORD, that thy children shall come again to their own border. 18- I have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning himself thus; Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke: turn thou me, and I shall be turned; for thou art the LORD my God. 19- Surely after that I was turned, I repented; and after that I was instructed, I smote upon my thigh: I was ashamed, yea, even confounded, because I did bear the reproach of my youth. 20- Is Ephraim my dear son? is he a pleasant child? for since I spake against him, I do earnestly remember him still: therefore my bowels are troubled for him; I will surely have mercy upon him, saith the LORD.

31.14.0.en: Ramah: a city in the north of Judea near the kingdom of Israel, near which Rachel the wife of Jacob died and was buried.

31.14.1.en: Rachel: the wife of Jacob, who signifies the mother of all the Jews.

31.14.2.en: Jeremiah expresses the sorrow of the captives, whom the Babylonians probably gathered in the region of Ramah before transferring them to Babylon and the surrounding countries, and their mothers, symbolized by Rachel, weep for them and cannot be comforted because they will not return to them. Matthew the Evangelist borrowed this prophecy at the massacre of the children of Bethlehem, because their mothers would not see them again (Mt 2:17, 18).

31.15.0.en: Thy work shall be rewarded: your tears and your supplications to God for your children.

31.15.1.en: God declares through the tongue of Jeremiah hope to all these mothers: that despite the might of Babylon, God will bring His people back.

31.16.2.en: God promises His people hope of the return, but not soon; rather at the end of the lives of those who are in Jerusalem, for the captives will return to their land within their borders after 70 years, and the aged, who have passed ninety or a hundred years of age, will receive them with joy.

31.17.0.en: Unaccustomed to the yoke: the animal trained in sound habits and conduct.

31.17.1.en: He borrows the name Ephraim, which represents the largest of the tribes, as a figure for all the Jews. The captives weep, and their kin also weep over them, and they humble themselves before God, feeling that their sins are the cause of this discipline, as Jeremiah informed them many times, so they ask God for feelings of repentance that they may obtain His mercies, because they walked in many sins and deviations like an untrained animal, and so deserved this discipline.

31.18.0.en: The people of God declare their regret and repentance: when the Babylonians attacked them and they saw the force of the treatment, they came to themselves and regretted their sins, and expressed their grief by striking the thigh, a custom that still occurs today in Egypt and the East, where people strike the cheeks and thigh in intense sorrow. They also remembered their former shameful sins, full of disgrace, and were ashamed of themselves.

31.19.0.en: Before the regret of the people of God, during their captivity, the fatherhood of God toward them appears, and He declares that His people are dear to Him, indeed the joy of His heart, so God's bowels yearn over them and He has mercy on them and brings them back from captivity.

31.19.1.en: God's tenderness toward you is wonderful: His heart does not change however much you sin, and He keeps waiting for you until you repent, then His bowels yearn over you, and He hastens to forgive you and embrace you, and restores you to your great place in His Church.

31.20.s.en: (4) Blessings for those returning from captivity

31.20.1.en: High heaps: a pillar of stone.

31.20.2.en: God likens His people to a virgin because He loves her as a bride, and says to her: set up stone pieces and stone pillars on the road from the countries to which you were carried captive as far as Jerusalem, so that your children returning from captivity to their land may be guided by them. It is a clear divine promise to bring His people back from captivity.

31.21.0.en: God requires His captive bride to turn back from her sins, and the captivity to be an opportunity for repentance, so that she turns from her apostasy from God; and God promises her to bring her back from captivity when she repents, and declares a strange fact as a clear prophecy, namely a woman shall compass a man, which has three meanings:

31.21.1.en: (1) The female is characterized by physical weakness, and the man, on the contrary, by strength. The female signifies the captive children of Israel, who are weak, and the man signifies strong Babylon. The situation will be reversed and the weak female will overcome the man, who returns by means of the Medes and Persians, who bring back the people of God with honor and strength, while Babylon is shattered, taken captive and enslaved.

31.21.2.en: (2) The female signifies the people of God who embrace the man, who is their God, when they repent and embrace their God, who lifts them up, saves them, and brings them back from captivity.

31.21.3.en: (3) The female signifies the Virgin Mary, who embraces in her womb the strongest man in the world, who is Christ her Son, to offer salvation to the whole world.

31.22.0.en: Among God's blessings to His people after the return from captivity is that righteousness, that is, God, dwells in their midst, so they, as His children, are characterized by righteousness, that is, purity and good works. Likewise Jerusalem and Judea are called the holy mountain, that is, they are characterized by steadfastness in God and spiritual strength.

31.23.0.en: He also promises them that they will sow their land, gather its fruit and be satisfied, and likewise shepherd their cattle so that they grow fat and increase in number; that is, their material prosperity increases. This signifies spiritual satisfaction, and Christ, His Apostles, His priests and His servants, who sow the word of God in people's hearts and care for the shepherding of their souls, enjoy fellowship with God.

31.24.0.en: God declares the joy of His heart at the rest of His people, and likens Himself to a man who awoke and saw the good of his people, so he rejoiced and slept with pleasure, delighting in his sleep. This is a prophecy about Christ, who died, that is, slept, on the Cross delighting in His sleep because He had completed our redemption.

31.24.1.en: God rejoices in your good, your walk with Him and all your virtues. So take care to walk uprightly, and try to acquire one virtue that you need, to rejoice the heart of God, so that you rejoice with Him.

31.25.0.en: God also promises that He Himself will sow man, that is, bless His children who return from captivity, multiply them and give them many blessings. Likewise He sows beast, that is, blesses and multiplies their cattle.

31.26.1.en: God likens Himself to a man who watches, that is, is occupied, concerned and persevering in disciplining His people with all the severe ways of discipline. His aim in this, of course, is their repentance, because of their violent insistence on sin; they needed this severe discipline, and they actually responded to the discipline of the captivity, and repented. Therefore God promises them that He will build not only their cities but their spiritual life with Him.

31.27.0.en: There was a common proverb that the fathers eat sour grapes, which are small, sharp-tasting grapes, and then the children's teeth are set on edge by this taste and knock against one another; that is, some of them thought that the discipline that came upon them in captivity was because of the sins of their fathers. God clearly declares that every person is responsible for his own sin and perishes because of it: if the fathers are wicked and the children righteous, the children do not perish, but if they imitate their fathers and become evil, they perish like their fathers. In sum, he means that the discipline that came upon them in captivity is because of their own evils, and the solution is repentance, and then God has mercy on them.

31.28.0.en: At the end of this chapter, God declares that He will make a covenant with His people returning from captivity. This covenant means a commitment from God, as one party, to care for His people, protect them and bless them, and the second party is His people, who are committed to obeying His commandments.

31.29.0.en: This covenant is new, and is not the first covenant which He made with His people when He delivered them from the bondage of Egypt and brought them through the Red Sea; this is a new covenant after He rescued them from the harshness of the Babylonian bondage. But even more, this covenant signifies the covenant which Christ makes with us by His blood on the Cross by His redemption of us.

31.30.0.en: The characteristics of this new covenant are:

31.30.1.en: 1- The people keep the Law of God and His commandments in their hearts; that is, they do not carry them out only literally but commit themselves to their spirit. This is what those returning from captivity did in part, and it was fulfilled even more in those who believe in Christ.

31.30.2.en: 2- They worship God and abandon the worship of idols; and in the New Covenant they are not occupied by material things and lusts, but by the love of Christ the Redeemer.

31.31.0.en: In the New Covenant God adds two other things:

31.31.1.en: 1- God becomes known and clear to all His children, so they discern that He is the only God and do not need anyone to teach them to abandon the idols. And in the Church the Holy Spirit descends on all the believers and guides them to the truth and to life with Him within His Church.

31.31.2.en: 2- God forgives all the repentant and lifts from them the debt of their sins, which He bore on the Cross; and in the case of those returning from captivity, He does not discipline them for their sins but blesses them with many material good things.

31.31.3.en: God wants to renew His covenants with you, and gives you more abundant blessings when you take care to keep His commandments and prefer Him to anything of your material affairs. Then He reveals to you, and you experience, an inexpressible delight which is a pledge of the glories of the Kingdom that have not entered into the heart of man.

31.32.0.en: Who divideth: the One who firmly restrains.

31.32.1.en: Roar: the waves surge with a strong sound.

31.32.2.en: God declares that He is steadfast in His promises with the whole creation. He appointed the sun to light the day, and the moon and the stars come after it to light the night, and He set boundaries for the sea so that it does not cover the dry land: it moves by the property of the tide, but despite the power of its waves its waters return inward by the property of the ebb. The One who set all these laws and governs them is God, who is able to do all things, and so He shows us His power by describing Himself as the Lord of hosts.

31.33.0.en: Because the order of nature is made firm by the power of God, He is also able to establish His people as a nation before Him throughout life; that is, this people will never become extinct. This actually happened, for the children of Israel remained as a nation throughout the Old Testament although exposed to the rule of the Medes and Persians, then the Greek and Roman states. But what is more important than this is that through Christ the Christians became the new Israel, the nation that lives not only throughout earthly time but extends into eternity.

31.34.0.en: God shows His pleasure and love for His people throughout life by proofs: it is impossible for man to measure the dimensions of heaven, however much he advances in science; he merely knows a little about it, but it is impossible for him to know everything about it and measure it. Likewise no one can know the foundations of the earth, that is, the depths of the globe; however much research advances, only some information about them is known. So, if it is impossible for anyone to measure heaven or to know the foundations of the earth, then God will not cast off His people but will keep them as a nation before Him until He takes them with Him in the Kingdom.

31.35.0.en: The tower of Hananeel: it is in the northeast of Jerusalem.

31.35.1.en: The corner gate: it is in the northwest of Jerusalem.

31.35.2.en: God affirms His establishing and keeping of His children who return from captivity by building for them their city Jerusalem, in which is His temple, from its east to its west.

31.36.0.en: The measuring line: the line used to set the stones and bricks in building; what is meant is the extent of the building.

31.36.1.en: The hill Gareb: a hill lying in the west of Jerusalem.

31.36.2.en: Goath: a region in the southwest of Jerusalem.

31.36.3.en: The valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes: it is the valley of Hinnom, or the one called the son of Hinnom, into which the remains of animals and all the waste of the city of Jerusalem were thrown to be burned there; it lies in the southwest of Jerusalem. From it the word Gehenna was taken.

31.36.4.en: The brook Kidron: a valley that passes around Jerusalem from its west, then its south, then turns toward its east.

31.36.5.en: The horse gate: one of the gates of Jerusalem, lying on the eastern side.

31.36.6.en: To complete God's affirmation of the rebuilding of Jerusalem, He mentions in detail many places in it through which the builders pass to rebuild it. After they begin from the northeast and extend toward the northwest (v. 38), they complete the western side and head toward the southwest, passing through the whole southern part until they reach the eastern region of Jerusalem; that is, all of Jerusalem is built.
